classification.difficultyReason: Interpret two graphical branches and translate open and closed endpoints into domain restrictions. The missing gradient is an unresolved source-data issue.

inlines.text: Find the rule of the graph given below.

spec.description: Coordinate axes with positive-direction arrows and x and y titles. A blue upward-curving left branch crosses the x-axis at the labelled −1 and terminates at an open circle at (0,−1). A rising blue straight ray begins at a filled circle at (0,1). Both branches have outward continuation arrows. No grid, guide lines, additional ticks or additional labelled points.
spec.mathematics: The left branch is reconstructed under the retained standard-parabola interpretation y=x²−1 for x<0. The right branch is a rising straight ray through (0,1), hence y=mx+1 for x≥0 with m>0; its exact gradient is not established by the labelled source. Its unlabelled drawing endpoint specifies schematic extent only.
spec.answerVisibility: The complete supplied graph remains visible in the question. No branch equations, gradient annotation or additional labelled point are added.

inlines.text: This assumes the left branch is quadratic. The labelled graph does not establish the right branch’s gradient
; another labelled point or an explicit gradient is needed.
Use the open and closed circles to determine which branch includes the break point.

answer.worked:
The break point is $x=0$. The open circle excludes $x=0$ from the left branch; the filled circle includes it in the right branch.

Under the standard-parabola interpretation, the left branch has vertex $(0,-1)$ and passes through $(-1,0)$, giving $y=x^2-1$ for $x<0$.

The right branch is a rising straight ray through $(0,1)$, so its rule is $y=mx+1$ for $x\ge0$, where $m>0$. The supplied labels do not determine the exact value of $m$.

Thus, under the quadratic interpretation, the supported family is
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2-1&\text{if }x<0,\\mx+1&\text{if }x\ge0.\end{cases}$$

The intended answer uses $m=2$:
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2-1&\text{if }x<0,\\2x+1&\text{if }x\ge0.\end{cases}$$
A second labelled point or an explicit gradient is needed to establish $m=2$ independently.
